spec_match.rationale: Implements the exact use case the change unblocks — HTML+CSS wrapped in foreignObject, drawn from a switchable blob:/data: source, then read back and exported — and its readback verdict comes from a real getImageData() call on every render.

interactive.rationale: Live HTML and CSS editors, a blob/data scheme switch that re-renders on change, a real toDataURL export that displays the produced PNG, and a fresh canvas per render because taint is permanent.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises composing styled HTML, drawing via a blob URL, exporting a PNG and seeing whether the canvas lets you — all present, including the taint refusal path.

edge_cases.rationale: Malformed-XHTML load failures get a dedicated explanation, the export failure branch reports the SecurityError with a suggested data: retry, the XHTML-namespace and inline-CSS gotchas are documented, and every render starts from a new canvas.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts the readback and the export (toDataURL) contracts separately with proper controls; on Chromium 141 the route ran 4 pass / 2 fail, the expected pre-156 split, agreeing with what this page itself reported at load.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): the page auto-rendered at load via blob and the console logged 'rendered via blob, readable=false' while the screenshot shows the receipt correctly drawn and the honest rose status 'Rendered via blob: but the canvas is tainted' with the SecurityError explanation — real observed pre-156 behaviour; the export button, scheme switch and editor edits could not be clicked headlessly.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert covers the rendered, export-succeeded and export-refused outcomes with scheme and readability payloads, and the console carries only the page's labelled logs.

design_system.rationale: Layout, editors and buttons all use design-system variables with correct button colour overrides, but the .status.ok state uses --accent-emerald (#0a8f5c) on --bg-stone (~3.7:1), below WCAG AA for normal-size bold text — the shared v156 palette finding.

accessibility.rationale: Textareas and radios are wrapped in labels, the outcome narrative is an aria-live=polite output, the status pairs text with an aria-hidden icon, the exported image carries meaningful alt text, and controls meet 44px targets.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: editors stack to one column on mobile, the canvas scales to container width, buttons and radios wrap without overflow, and the same auto-render verdict appears on both classes.

openQuestions.title: Empty exported-image slot renders as a broken image
openQuestions.detail: The #saved img has no src until an export succeeds, so browsers paint a broken-image placeholder with the alt text in a bordered box (visible in the desktop capture). Hiding the img (or the whole 'Exported image' section) until an export succeeds, or using a neutral placeholder panel, would avoid shipping a permanently-broken-looking element on every pre-156 browser where export always fails via blob.

openQuestions.title: Export success overwrites the taint verdict in the status line
openQuestions.detail: A successful export calls setStatus('ok', 'Exported'), replacing the render verdict; after switching schemes and exporting, the status no longer says which scheme produced the shown PNG. Keeping the render verdict and reporting export outcome only in the detail output (or including the scheme in the export status) would preserve the causal story the demo is telling.

openQuestions.title: Emerald ok-status text misses WCAG AA on stone
openQuestions.detail: Shared palette finding: --accent-emerald on --bg-stone is ~3.7:1 for the bold status text, below the 4.5:1 AA requirement (invariant #5). Same as the sibling pages; best fixed once at palette level.

summary: The strongest runtime evidence in this feature: on this pre-156 Chromium 141 build the page auto-rendered its receipt via a blob URL at load, the drawing succeeded, and the readback honestly failed — console logged 'rendered via blob, readable=false' and the UI showed the rose 'canvas is tainted' status with the SecurityError explanation and the data:-workaround pointer, which is exactly the story the feature exists to end. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v156/svg-foreignobject-does-not-taint-the-canvas-for-blob-urls/html-to-canvas/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots, DOM dump, clean console; feature /conformance/ route 4 pass / 2 fail as expected pre-156). Export, scheme-switch and editor interactions could not be clicked headlessly and are judged from wiring. Remaining questions are cosmetic: the broken-image placeholder before any export, and status-line overwrites.
